metadata.no_mutation_note: No supervisor start/doctor/clear-recovery/record-manifest run; no push/merge/PR; no campaign/runtime/journal mutation. Provider live canaries: NOT_RUN (0 of 8 authorized calls used - see canary_note).

canary_note: Live provider canaries (F1 json-schema, F3 permission stdio round-trip, F4 two-message max-turns, F6 codex read-only) were NOT_RUN. Rationale: Fable 5 is capped and a live claude/codex round-trip on the exact production argv risks the same capped-default capability poisoning seen in journey-4 (M0-T132 doctor --live), and the permission-wrapper + json-schema contracts are owner-gated live-CLI acts. The behavioral contracts they would test (C6/C8-structured-output/C7) are adjudicated here by REPRODUCED static probes against production validators + official-doc comparison, which is decisive for the FAIL findings. Exact standalone owner commands to run them are in STABILIZATION_REPAIR_PLAN.md section 6.

contracts.title: Canonical controller source / stale-main risk
contracts.observed: CONTROLLER_UPDATE_RUNBOOK.md installs the controller delta from origin/main of a separate clone; origin/main is 0/567 behind control and its tools/agent_supervisor has 63 files vs 169 on control (missing github_flow.py/launch_seam.py/command_docs.py). No canonical source+SHA defined; retired ids (wt-m0t063, M0-T063, M0-T127) hardcoded.
contracts.expected: One canonical controller source pinned to a SHA that actually contains the shipping supervisor code; install verified byte-for-byte against a manifest.
contracts.probe: git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD ; git ls-tree -r origin/main tools/agent_supervisor/ | wc -l ; read docs/CONTROLLER_UPDATE_RUNBOOK.md:69-72
contracts.defect: Following the approved-looking runbook installs a controller 567 commits behind live; syntax checks pass because all flags are legal.
contracts.positive_test: doc-lint: the runbook's install ref must resolve to a commit containing tools/agent_supervisor/github_flow.py
contracts.mutant_test: flip the install ref back to origin/main -> lint fails
contracts.depends_on: C14 (canonical integration ref must exist first)

contracts.title: Generated PowerShell command semantics + $LASTEXITCODE binding
contracts.observed: supervisor_command_doc_check.py only argparse-parses commands and checks pinned-flag TOKEN presence; it never resolves referenced paths, never binds task-id/packet/worktree/branch/HEAD/queue values, never detects stale origin/main, and never parses or executes PowerShell. The Windows CI job runs every step via shell:bash and captures no $LASTEXITCODE.
contracts.expected: A command-doc guard that verifies the semantics that break a live start (resolvable paths, worktree/branch/HEAD/packet binding) and a Windows job that actually parses PowerShell + captures raw $LASTEXITCODE.
contracts.defect: check_worktree_binding exists (command_docs.py:337-361) but the CI entry never calls it; validate_command checks flag-token presence only (:313-315). Operator packages can be semantically wrong (wrong worktree, retired paths, stale source) and still report 12/0.
contracts.positive_test: a runbook start whose --worktree mismatches the packet must FAIL the doc-check
contracts.mutant_test: point --worktree at the primary checkout -> must FAIL (today: passes)

contracts.title: Executable identity / updater freeze / preflight-vs-dispatch drift
contracts.observed: process.py identifies the ~265 MB Claude CLI by a partial hash (first 1 MiB + file size, label sha256_head+size) above a 64 MiB threshold; the executable is never re-hashed at dispatch against an admitted value; DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER is set at launch but the updater/version is not an admission-frozen field.
contracts.expected: Full-content digest at admission, re-verified byte-identical before every dispatch; a swapped/updated binary halts the run.
contracts.defect: A binary that changes after the first 1 MiB while preserving size evades the admitted digest; no dispatch-time drift re-check.
contracts.positive_test: executable_identity on a 100 MiB file returns digest_kind == sha256 (full)
contracts.mutant_test: two 100 MiB files identical in first 1 MiB and equal in size but differing at 2 MiB must produce different digests (today they collide)

contracts.title: Effective Claude/Codex host inventory binding (recert gap)
contracts.observed: The controller manifest binds only the supervisor package files (*.py/schemas/prompts/config.toml/launchers/README) plus the external config.toml. The repo-root .claude/settings.json (model=fable-5, fallbackModel=[opus-4-8], effortLevel=xhigh, hooks, deniedMcpServers, permissions.deny=[mcp__*]), .claude/hooks/*, CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*, skills, subagents, plugins, MCP inventory, and the claude executable digest are ALL unbound. build_argv pins no --settings/--strict-mcp-config, so the worker reads effort/model/hooks/MCP/CLAUDE.md from ambient filesystem state.
contracts.expected: Admission binds every input that changes worker behavior; any host-inventory change forces recertification.
contracts.defect: Host-local settings/hooks/MCP/plugins/model-default can change worker behavior AFTER recertification without invalidating the admitted identity (the exact class of defect journey-4 hit with the model default).
contracts.positive_test: editing .claude/settings.json after record-manifest -> verify_manifest_with_config returns ok=False
contracts.mutant_test: flip effortLevel xhigh->low or add an MCP server -> verification halts (today stays green)

contracts.title: Exact-child-env model identity + Claude/Codex/GitHub auth
contracts.observed: The child env allowlist preserves HOME/USERPROFILE but drops APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/SSH_AUTH_SOCK/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY. Preflight proves the executables EXIST (codex --version/--help under ambient env; anonymous git ls-remote in the SUPERVISOR env), not that the exact child env can AUTHENTICATE to Claude/Codex/GitHub. Worker/reviewer model identity is checked only after-the-fact, not pre-dispatch (exact provider-reported id is verified only for the orchestrator role).
contracts.expected: Preflight proves the exact child env authenticates to all three externals and verifies the provider-reported model id before unattended dispatch.
contracts.probe: read process.py:103-108/218-247 ; preflight.py:95-270 ; capability_probe.py:53-55/84-102 ; start_gate.py:112-127 ; claude_runner.py:1791-1794/1909-1920 ; cli.py:2795
contracts.defect: Claude, Codex, or GitHub may fail only AFTER dispatch (existence != auth); dropping APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA may itself break Windows keychain-based auth for the child.
contracts.files_functions: tools/agent_supervisor/preflight.py (add codex + github auth probes under the EXACT child env) ; process.DEFAULT_ENV_ALLOWLIST
contracts.positive_test: codex-auth preflight returns VERIFIED only on a codex exec round-trip authenticated under minimal_env()
contracts.mutant_test: remove the codex credential source -> probe FAILS (today nothing fails until runtime)

contracts.title: --permission-prompt-tool stdio real behavior
contracts.observed: The runner passes literal 'stdio' to --permission-prompt-tool and implements the permission protocol privately (reads control_request off stdout, writes build_control_response to stdin). The response wrapper is self-declared UNVERIFIED against the live CLI (CONTROL_RESPONSE_WRAPPER_VERIFIED=False) and there is NO per-permission-response deadline (only the 900s wall). Official docs define --permission-prompt-tool as naming an MCP tool, not 'stdio'.
contracts.expected: The value given triggers a routing the installed CLI honors, and every permission request resolves within a bounded time; the wrapper is proven against the live CLI.
contracts.probe: read claude_runner.py:79-98/321/364-368/1427-1432/1691-1719 ; BLOCKED_OWNER_GATE for the live round-trip (owner-gated, capped model)
contracts.defect: The permission bridge depends on measured-private behavior the code itself marks unverified; a CLI update can silently break tool approval, and a hung broker rides the 900s wall.
contracts.files_functions: tools/agent_supervisor/claude_runner.py:_answer_control_request / run_unit read loop (add response deadline) ; tools/agent_supervisor/preflight.py (live round-trip probe to flip CONTROL_RESPONSE_WRAPPER_VERIFIED)
contracts.positive_test: fake CLI emits can_use_tool; assert an exact control_response allow/deny frame round-trips
contracts.mutant_test: fake CLI never emits the request / ignores the response; assert the unit fails closed within a bounded permission deadline (survives today)

contracts.title: Controller-owned total turn/call budget vs per-message --max-turns
contracts.observed: --max-turns is set to turn_budget.total_turns and enforced per stream-json message. run_unit has NO controller-side cumulative turn/call counter; a reserved second message (the checkpoint-starvation turn) receives a fresh full --max-turns allowance, so a unit can consume ~2x total_turns. stdin is closed on per-message completion, not on a global budget.
contracts.expected: A bounded unit consumes at most total_turns model turns end-to-end; when spent, the controller closes stdin.
contracts.defect: The claimed per-unit turn bound can be roughly doubled by the reserved message; the 'do not start new tool use' guidance is untrusted prompt text, not an enforced bound.
contracts.files_functions: tools/agent_supervisor/claude_runner.py:run_unit (cumulative turn counter + stdin close at total_turns)
contracts.positive_test: worker uses all working turns, emits no checkpoint, gets the reserved turn; total model turns <= total_turns
contracts.mutant_test: worker ignores the reserved-turn instruction and keeps calling tools; stdin closes at the global budget (survives today up to a second full allowance)

contracts.title: Claude checkpoint schema enforcement + controller correlation
contracts.observed: validate_checkpoint accepts int summary/proposed_next_action, empty run_id/task_id/checkpoint_id/claude_session_id/schema_version, claims='not-a-list', changed_files wrong shape, usage=[]. from_dict is presence-only; validate() checks only status membership + usage!=0/None. The runtime validator is weaker than schemas/claude_checkpoint.schema.json (which has minLength:1 + per-field types). No correlation of run_id/task_id/session_id/checkpoint_id to controller-observed values. M0-T133's checkpoint_envelope fixes only the 4 git-state fields.
contracts.expected: Runtime validation at least as strong as the JSON schema (types, minLength>=1 ids, supported schema_version) PLUS exact correlation of the four identity fields to controller values.
contracts.probe: python -c import claude_runner; validate_checkpoint({...malformed...}) -> reproduced ACCEPTED; read models.py:110-128/175-182 ; schemas/claude_checkpoint.schema.json:23-37 ; loop.py:2043
contracts.defect: A model-invented or corrupt checkpoint (wrong types, empty ids, wrong run/session) enters the controller as valid state; journey-5's missing-fields defect is a subset the envelope patched, not the envelope contract.
contracts.positive_test: valid typed checkpoint with matching controller identity passes
contracts.mutant_test: summary=int / empty run_id / mismatched claude_session_id / schema_version='v999' each raises invalid_checkpoint

contracts.title: Codex decision schema + HEAD/origin/evidence binding
contracts.observed: validate_decision accepts decision=COMPLETE with verified_repo_head='definitely-not-a-sha', verified_origin_main='', model_used='', verified_facts=[{}], evidence_refs=[{}]. _reject_wrong_types checks only str/list shapes; REQUIRED_BY_DECISION['COMPLETE'] requires only evidence_refs nonempty. No SHA-format check, no origin_main nonempty, no object-content check, and NO controller-git parameter -> no equality binding. The SHAs never reach loop.py/next_task.py advancement.
contracts.expected: For COMPLETE: verified_repo_head is a full SHA, verified_origin_main nonempty, verified_facts/evidence_refs nonempty resolvable objects, AND verified_repo_head/verified_origin_main EQUAL controller-collected git.head/git.origin_main in the frozen packet.
contracts.probe: python -c import codex_reviewer; validate_decision({...COMPLETE...}) -> reproduced ACCEPTED; read codex_reviewer.py:141/161-163/196-245/710 ; next_task.py:702-725
contracts.defect: A reviewer can COMPLETE the wrong or unverified state; the git/evidence equality lives only as unenforced model-facing prompt text.
contracts.mutant_test: bad-SHA head / empty origin_main / head != packet-head / evidence_refs=[{}] each raises

contracts.title: Queue/packet/worktree/branch/HEAD/status binding
contracts.observed: Eligibility binds packet-content digest, task_id, worktree/repo PATHS, status=='claimed', deps-accepted, and a carried branch string - but never reads/binds the worktree's git HEAD, an expected starting HEAD, or a working-tree cleanliness/status digest. Eligibility IS re-run per successor immediately before dispatch, but the HEAD/clean checks do not exist to re-run. The owner-typed first task is not status-gated at all.
contracts.expected: Each entry bound to task_id + packet digest + canonical repo/worktree + exact branch + expected starting HEAD + current HEAD + status digest; a fresh successor required CLEAN at exact HEAD, distinct from a resumed dirty task.
contracts.defect: A stale, dirty, or wrong-HEAD successor worktree can enter under a valid task id; branch is re-bound onto args but never verified against live git.
contracts.files_functions: tools/agent_supervisor/next_task.py:TaskQueueEntry/evaluate_eligibility (add expected_starting_head + status digest + live HEAD/porcelain check via read-only GitRunner)
contracts.positive_test: clean successor at expected HEAD on the named branch dispatches
contracts.mutant_test: dirty tree / moved HEAD / wrong branch each skipped with an audited code

contracts.title: Fresh remote observation vs stale tracking refs
contracts.observed: EvidenceCollector defaults allow_remote_reads=False and reads LOCAL origin/main (rev-parse origin/main; ahead_behind vs origin/main) with no proof of when it was last fetched. No git ls-remote head+timestamp binding before a decision depends on remote state; refresh_remote returns 'not_configured' unless enabled and even then only fetch --prune.
contracts.expected: Any decision depending on remote state binds an observed remote head (ls-remote) + observation timestamp, or fails closed / declares staleness.
contracts.defect: git.origin_main / ahead_behind in the frozen packet can be silently stale with no recorded age, feeding a COMPLETE decision.
contracts.files_functions: tools/agent_supervisor/evidence.py:EvidenceCollector (ls-remote observation + observed_at_utc; mark origin_main STALE/UNVERIFIED absent a fresh observation)
contracts.positive_test: with a fresh ls-remote observation the packet carries remote_head+timestamp matching local
contracts.mutant_test: local origin/main behind the ls-remote head flags stale rather than silently passing

contracts.title: Raw gate-result integrity (unpiped exit capture)
contracts.observed: No central gate-runner records raw argv + raw exit code + stdout/stderr digests to JSON; gate reports transcribe terminal text ('exit 0'/'failures 0'). M0-T133's producer + G2 self-check again misstated modularity as exit 0 while the true unpiped exit is 1 - the same class as the M0-T130 'modularity_check | tail' false green.
contracts.expected: Every gate verdict derives from a captured raw exit code, never prose; a display filter may run only after the raw result is stored.
contracts.probe: python tools/modularity_check.py --check (unpiped) -> RAW_EXIT captured; read M0-T133-G2-self-check.md:20-24, M0-T133-G3-code-review.md:29-38, M0-T133-G4-qa-review.md:26-32
contracts.defect: The evidence-generation process can convert a failing gate into an accepted-looking record; recurred across M0-T130 and M0-T133. NOTE: at the audited 6f5d12a6 modularity is exit 1 (1432/1410); the local unpushed renewal (b7b203d2) makes it exit 0 at 1435, but the owner directed split-not-renew (R474/R475), so the launch-critical fix is the split + a central gate-runner.
contracts.files_functions: new tools/gate_runner.py (subprocess.run(argv) -> {argv, returncode, stdout_sha256, stderr_sha256} JSON); gate skills consume the JSON not pasted text
contracts.positive_test: runner records exit 1 for a failing check
contracts.mutant_test: wrap the command in | tail / Tee-Object -> recorded returncode stays the tool's, not the pipe's

contracts.title: Process containment, timeout classification, EOF ordering, recovery
contracts.observed: ONE fixed 900s wall watchdog, no phase-specific deadlines (startup/first-event/per-turn/permission-response/stream-drain). CONTAINMENT PASS: Windows Job Object default kill-on-close, no breakaway, membership proven via IsProcessInJob, honest taskkill /T /F fallback (a grandchild spawned between enumerate and kill can escape on the fallback path, acknowledged, not proven-zero). RESULT/EOF/drain ordering handled. RECOVERY PASS: PAUSED_RECOVERY reachable from ~15 states and exitable by the real owner_cleared_pause->PREFLIGHT command.
contracts.expected: Phase-specific deadlines + liveness predicates; and a post-kill descendant-enumeration proof on the fallback path.
contracts.defect: One number cannot distinguish healthy-and-draining, waiting-for-MCP, model-retry, and never-arriving; healthy work can be killed or dead work can stall ~15 min. Containment and recovery are sound.
contracts.files_functions: tools/agent_supervisor/claude_runner.py:run_unit.watchdog (phased deadlines) ; tools/agent_supervisor/process.py:ProcessContainer.terminate_all (post-terminate descendant-zero proof on taskkill path)
contracts.positive_test: worker emits its first event slowly then completes; a first-event deadline fires independently of the 900s total
contracts.mutant_test: worker spawns a detached grandchild then exits; assert zero descendants remain post-unit (survives today on the taskkill fallback)

contracts.title: Real GitHub lifecycle topology + worker-branch-to-integration safety
contracts.observed: The entire GitHub flow is SHADOW-ONLY: github_flow.py performs no real push/PR/merge (all effects cross an injected GitHubRunner Protocol; github_pr_merge deliberately excluded from MODELED_EFFECTS); push_policy.py sets NO_PUSH_EXECUTION_IN_THIS_PHASE=True; project-control acceptance stays manual; the R595 activation gate is never lifted. TOPOLOGY: ls-remote shows only control/*, task branches, and main - NO integration/develop/staging branch exists. Control is 0/567 ahead of main with ~1151 changed files, so a task branch cut from control shares that 567-commit lineage; a PR with base:main would enumerate all 567 commits + the task's own.
contracts.expected: A real adapter targets an integration branch at/near the task's merge-base so a correlated PR shows only the task's commits; production push/PR/check/merge/acceptance execution exists.
contracts.probe: read github_flow.py:3/21/56-64/709-724 ; push_policy.py:11-13/51/75-79 ; loop.py:2267-2269 ; README ; git ls-remote --heads origin
contracts.defect: The end-to-end ordinary-work lifecycle the owner requires (R472: push -> correlated PR -> CI -> green merge -> ledger) cannot be performed today: the execution does not exist AND no sane PR target branch exists. Reconciling the 567-commit control<->main divergence is an undefined large merge and a prerequisite architecture decision.
contracts.files_functions: establish canonical integration branch ; real GitHubRunner impl (github_flow.py:719 base=integration) ; reconcile control<->main divergence
contracts.positive_test: a PR built from a task branch off the integration ref shows only the task's commits
contracts.mutant_test: set base=main -> PR commit-count assertion fails

smallest_architecture_decision_required: Resolve the control<->main branch topology BEFORE any launch-contract repair: designate one canonical integration branch and decide how the 567-commit control/D-024-fable-codex-loop divergence becomes the mainline the loop pushes to and merges into (Option A: reconcile/merge control into main so main is current and task branches PR into main; Option B: promote a protected integration branch at the current control head as the mainline and reconcile main separately). This single decision unblocks C1 (canonical controller source) and C14 (PR base topology) and is the precondition for the end-to-end ordinary-work lifecycle target (R472). Everything else is large but ordinary in-house engineering.
